title: Hanna photographs the desert
topic: A photographer named Hanna travels through a desert: dunes in the evening light, a night in tents near a well, a caravan at dawn, packing for the journey home
tail_E: For the last stretch through the dunes the guide helps her onto the back of a kneeling
target_note: 'camel' is predictable only from the desert context (desert, dunes, sand, a well, a caravan in unit 9): the riding animal that kneels to be mounted in the dunes is the camel. The word does not occur in the units or the tail (the caravan is never said to consist of camels), and neither does its German equivalent 'Kamel'. ' camel' is a single Pythia token (id 46493). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' camel') = 0.34 on the all-English rendering, rank 1 (next: ' horse' 0.12). Without 'kneeling' ('... she rides on the back of a') ' camel' is still rank 1 but only p = 0.06 against ' car', so the participle was added to sharpen the prediction.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (DEV03A, photographer Hanna, development family)
notes: Development family (dose/threshold choice only, never for confirmation). Ten units: Hanna travels through the desert with her camera; the sun burns on the sand; a local guide leads her to a dune; Hanna photographs the dunes in the evening light; the wind carries sand across the track; the travellers sleep in tents near a well; the stars shine over the desert; Hanna changes the lens before sunrise; a caravan reaches the well at dawn; Hanna packs her bags for the journey home. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Hanna), other people (a local guide, the travellers - plural, a caravan) and natural objects (the sun, the wind, the stars - plural), so that C3 switches cross singular and plural subject-verb agreement; units 2 and 7 have bare intransitive predicates (burns/brennt, shine/leuchten). No separable verbs ('erreicht', 'wechselt', 'bringt' are simple verbs). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Units 1 and 10 read naturally in English, unit 9 in German; unit 10 closes the trip.
